questions.question: On 29 April 2025, which new facility was launched by the National Center for Sports Science and Research (NCSSR) to revolutionise athlete rehabilitation in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Return to Play Facility**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **29 April 2025**, the **National Center for Sports Science and Research (NCSSR)** launched the **Return to Play Facility** to revolutionize the way Indian athletes recover from injuries and transition back to active competition.
 
• The primary objective of this facility is to provide a **scientific and data-driven approach** to rehabilitation, ensuring that athletes do not just recover but return to their respective sports at **peak performance levels**.
 
• This facility is designed to cater specifically to **elite athletes**, **national campers**, and participants in the **Khelo India** schemes, reducing the dependency on overseas rehabilitation centers.
 
• The **Return to Play Facility** utilizes advanced **sports science** technologies, including **biomechanical monitoring** and **physiological assessment tools**, to track an athlete's progress throughout the recovery cycle.
 
• It bridges the critical gap between medical clearance after an injury and the athlete's ability to withstand the **high-intensity physical demands** of professional sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Center for Sports Science and Research (NCSSR):**
 
 
• The **NCSSR** is a key initiative under the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, Government of India, aimed at providing high-level scientific support to athletes.
 
• It functions as a hub for **sports medicine**, **sports nutrition**, and **sports psychology**, working in close coordination with the **Sports Authority of India (SAI)**.
 
 
 
• **Athlete Rehabilitation Process:**
 
 
• Modern rehabilitation involves more than just physiotherapy; it includes **strength and conditioning**, **load management**, and **mental health support** to ensure holistic recovery.
 
• The **Return to Play** protocol is a standardized phase-wise progression that ensures an athlete meets specific **functional criteria** before returning to the field.
 
 
 
• **Significance in the Indian Context:**
 
 
• By establishing world-class facilities like this, India aims to improve its medal prospects in the **Olympic Games**, **Asian Games**, and **Commonwealth Games**.
 
• The facility helps in the early identification of **injury-prone movements**, thereby acting as a preventive tool to prolong the careers of Indian sportspersons.
 
• It represents a shift toward a **professionalized sports ecosystem** where every aspect of an athlete's health is managed by **certified specialists** and **modern equipment**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The launch of this facility coincides with India's increasing focus on **sports technology** and the integration of **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** in performance tracking.
 
• The **Return to Play Facility** is expected to operate in collaboration with various **High-Performance Centers (HPCs)** across the country to create a unified **athlete management system**.
 
• Key technologies deployed include **anti-gravity treadmills**, **isokinetic dynamometers**, and **cryotherapy chambers** to speed up the healing and strengthening processes.
</ul

questions.question: The municipal corporation of which city launched India’s first QR-Based Digital House Address System in July 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indore Municipal Corporation (IMC)** achieved a significant milestone by launching India’s first **QR-Based Digital House Address System** in **July 2025**.
 
• This innovative system assigns a unique **Digital Address** to every household in the city, which is accessible through a **QR code** plate installed at the entrance of the property.
 
• The primary objective of this project is to simplify **urban navigation** and improve the efficiency of **municipal service delivery**, such as waste management and emergency response.
 
• The **Digital Address** system integrates various datasets, including **Property Tax** records, water connection details, and **Geospatial** coordinates, into a single scannable interface.
 
• By implementing this system, **Indore** has become the first city in India to transition from traditional, often confusing physical addresses to a precise, **digitized location framework**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Smart Cities Mission:**
 
 
• The **Smart Cities Mission** was launched by the **Government of India** in **June 2015** to promote sustainable and inclusive cities.
 
• **Indore** has consistently been a frontrunner in this mission, utilizing **Information and Communication Technology (ICT)** to enhance the quality of government services.
 
 
 
• **Indore's Cleanliness Legacy:**
 
 
• **Indore**, located in **Madhya Pradesh**, is widely recognized for its cleanliness and has been ranked as India's **cleanest city** for multiple consecutive years in the **Swachh Survekshan** survey.
 
• The introduction of the **QR-based system** further strengthens its **Solid Waste Management** tracking by ensuring that every house is covered during collection rounds.
 
 
 
• **Digital India Initiative:**
 
 
• The **Digital India** campaign, launched in **2015**, aims to ensure that government services are available to citizens electronically by improving online infrastructure and internet connectivity.
 
• Digital addressing is a subset of this vision, facilitating easier **E-commerce** deliveries, postal services, and **Logistics** management.
 
 
 
• **Technological Integration:**
 
 
• The system utilizes **GIS (Geographic Information System)** mapping to provide exact locations, which is particularly useful for **Ambulance** and **Fire Services** in navigating narrow urban lanes.
 
• It also helps the **Municipal Corporation** in identifying unauthorized constructions and ensuring accurate **Property Valuation** and revenue collection.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Benefits of the System:**
 
 
• **Ease of Navigation:** Visitors and service providers can find exact locations using a simple **Unique Digital Code** or scanning the **QR code**.
 
• **Emergency Efficiency:** Reduces response time for **Emergency Services** like the **Police** or **Disaster Management** teams by eliminating address ambiguity.
 
• **Data Centralization:** All civic amenities linked to a property are unified under one **Digital ID**, promoting transparency in **Governance**.
 
 
 
• **Future Scope:**
 
 
• Following **Indore's** success, other major cities like **Hyderabad**, **Jaipur**, and **Bengaluru** are expected to adopt similar **Digital Addressing** frameworks under the **National Urban Digital Mission**.

questions.question: Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2025, conducted under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), evaluated how many cities across India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**130 cities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan** is an initiative by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** to rank cities on the basis of implementation of activities approved under the **City Action Plan** and air quality improvement.
 
• Under the **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)**, the survey for **2025** evaluated **130 cities** across India to measure their progress in reducing air pollution levels.
 
• The assessment is based on various parameters including **solid waste management**, **road dust management**, **management of construction and demolition waste**, **control of vehicular emissions**, and **industrial pollution**.
 
• Cities are ranked based on the self-assessment reports submitted on the **PRANA portal**, which are further vetted by a technical team and third-party agencies.
 
• The **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan** aims to promote healthy competition among cities and encourage them to take proactive steps toward achieving the targets of the **NCAP**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP):**
 
 
• Launched in **January 2019**, the **NCAP** is a long-term, time-bound, national-level strategy to tackle the air pollution problem across the country in a comprehensive manner.
 
• The initial target was to achieve a **20% to 30% reduction** in **Particulate Matter (PM10 and PM2.5)** concentrations by **2024**, keeping **2017** as the base year for comparison.
 
• The **Government of India** later updated the target to achieve a **40% reduction** in particulate matter levels in targeted cities by the year **2026**.
 
 
 
• **Categorization of Cities:**
 
 
• For the purpose of ranking, cities are divided into three categories based on their **2011 Census population**.
 
• **Category 1**: Cities with a population of more than **10 lakhs** (Million-plus cities).
 
• **Category 2**: Cities with a population between **3 lakhs and 10 lakhs**.
 
• **Category 3**: Cities with a population of less than **3 lakhs**.
 
 
 
• **PRANA Portal:**
 
 
• **PRANA** stands for **Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in Non-Attainment cities**.
 
• It serves as a platform to monitor the implementation of the **NCAP** and provides real-time information on air quality and the status of various city-level action plans.
 
• It facilitates transparency and accountability by allowing the **MoEFCC** and the public to track the progress of **131 non-attainment cities**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Non-Attainment Cities:** These are cities that have consistently failed to meet the **National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)** for **PM10** or **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2)** over a period of **five years**.
 
• **Funding:** The **NCAP** provides dedicated funds to these cities to implement measures like installing **Electric Vehicle (EV)** charging stations, increasing green cover, and upgrading mechanical street sweeping machines.
 
• **Incentives:** Cities performing well in the **Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan** are awarded **cash prizes** and trophies to further motivate local urban bodies to prioritize **environmental health**.
 
• **Air Quality Index (AQI):** While the Sarvekshan looks at action taken, the **AQI** remains the standard daily tool for communicating the health of the air to the public, ranging from **'Good' (0-50)** to **'Severe' (above 400)**.
</ul

questions.question: Recognised for excellence in chess, which individual was honoured with the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gukesh Dommaraju**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gukesh Dommaraju**, popularly known as **Gukesh D**, was selected for the prestigious **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** in **2025** in recognition of his extraordinary achievements in the field of **Chess**.
 
• He created history by becoming the **youngest-ever challenger** for the **World Chess Championship** title after winning the **FIDE Candidates Tournament** held in **Toronto**, **Canada**, in **April 2024**.
 
• He played a instrumental role in India winning its first-ever **Gold Medal** in the **Open Category** at the **45th Chess Olympiad** held in **Budapest**, **Hungary**, in **September 2024**, where he also won an individual **Gold Medal** on the **first board**.
 
• The **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna** is the **highest sporting honor** in India, awarded annually by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** for spectacular and most outstanding performance in the field of sports over a period of **four years**.
 
• Gukesh became a **Grandmaster** at the age of **12 years, 7 months, and 17 days**, making him the **third-youngest** person in history to achieve this title at that time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Harmanpreet Singh**: 
 
 
• He is the **captain** of the **Indian Men's National Hockey Team**.
 
• Under his leadership, India won the **Bronze Medal** at the **Paris 2024 Olympics**.
 
• He was the **top scorer** of the **Paris Olympics** hockey tournament with **10 goals** and is widely regarded as one of the best **drag-flickers** in the world.
 
 
 
• **Praveen Kumar**: 
 
 
• He is a celebrated Indian **Para-athlete** specializing in the **High Jump**.
 
• He clinched the **Gold Medal** in the **Men's High Jump T64** event at the **Paris 2024 Paralympics** with an **Asian Record** jump of **2.08 meters**.
 
 
 
• **Anish Sarkar**: 
 
 
• He is a chess prodigy from **West Bengal** who made headlines in late **2024**.
 
• At the age of **3 years, 8 months, and 19 days**, he became the **youngest-ever FIDE-rated player** in history, surpassing the previous record.
 
 
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award**:
 
 
• The award was formerly known as the **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award** and was renamed in **August 2021**.
 
• The first recipient of this award was the chess legend **Viswanathan Anand** in the year **1991-92**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** carries a cash prize of **Rs. 25 lakh**, a **medallion**, and a **certificate**.
 
• **Gukesh D** reached a peak **FIDE live rating** of over **2790** in **2024**, solidifying his position among the **top 5** chess players globally.
 
• In **2023**, he surpassed **Viswanathan Anand** to become the **top-ranked Indian player** in the **FIDE rating list**, ending Anand's **37-year** reign as India's **number one**.
 
• The award ceremony usually takes place at the **Rashtrapati Bhavan**, where the **President of India** confers the honors upon the athletes.
</ul

questions.question: The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order (Amendment) Bill, 2023 amends the Constitution (Scheduled Caste) Order 1950 with respect to which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order (Amendment) Bill, 2023** was introduced and passed by the **Parliament of India** to amend the **Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950**, specifically in its application to the state of **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• The primary objective of the bill is to include the **Mahara** and **Mahra** communities as synonyms for the **Mehra**, **Mahar**, and **Ganda** communities in the **Scheduled Castes** list of **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• The **Lok Sabha** passed the bill on **July 24, 2023**, and the **Rajya Sabha** gave its approval on **August 9, 2023**, during the **Monsoon Session**.
 
• This amendment ensures that members of these communities can avail of the benefits meant for **Scheduled Castes** in the state, including **reservation** in educational institutions and government jobs.
 
• The bill was moved by the **Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment**, **Shri Virendra Kumar**, to rectify discrepancies in the existing list. ***Hence, the correct answer is Chhattisgarh.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 341 of the Constitution:** 
 
 
• This article empowers the **President** to specify the castes, races, or tribes which shall be deemed to be **Scheduled Castes** in relation to a particular **State** or **Union Territory**.
 
• Once the initial list is notified by the **President**, any inclusion or exclusion from the list can only be done by an **Act of Parliament**.
 
 
 
• **The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950:** 
 
 
• This is the foundational **Presidential Order** that lists the various castes eligible for affirmative action in **India**.
 
• It has been amended several times over the decades (e.g., **1956**, **1976**, and **2002**) to reflect changing social dynamics and administrative corrections.
 
 
 
• **The Process of Inclusion:** 
 
 
• The process begins with a recommendation from the concerned **State Government**.
 
• It is then vetted by the **Registrar General of India (RGI)** and the **National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC)**.
 
• After their concurrence, the proposal is placed before the **Union Cabinet** and finally introduced as a **Bill** in **Parliament**.
 
 
 
• **Chhattisgarh State Context:** 
 
 
• The state of **Chhattisgarh** was carved out of **Madhya Pradesh** on **November 1, 2000**.
 
• Since its formation, there have been several demands to include phonetic variations of existing **Scheduled Castes** and **Scheduled Tribes** to ensure legitimate beneficiaries are not excluded due to spelling errors or local nomenclature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment:** This ministry is the nodal agency at the **Central Government** level for the welfare of **Scheduled Castes**.
 
• **Impact of the 2023 Bill:** By adding the **Mahara** and **Mahra** communities, the government addressed a long-standing demand for **social justice**, as these groups were historically denied benefits despite sharing the same socio-economic status as the **Mahar** or **Ganda** communities.
 
• **National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC):** Established under **Article 338**, this constitutional body monitors safeguards provided for **Scheduled Castes** and participated in the consultative process for this **2023 Amendment**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following schemes aims at fostering innovation & technology development in defence and aerospace by engaging start-ups, MSMEs, academic institutes under the management of the Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO)?

options.text: Acing Development of Innovative Technologies with iDEX

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Innovations for Defence Excellence**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX)** was launched by the **Prime Minister** of India in **April 2018** during the **DefExpo**.
 
• It serves as the flagship initiative of the **Ministry of Defence** to encourage **innovation** and **technology development** specifically for the **Defence and Aerospace** sectors.
 
• The scheme is managed and funded by the **Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO)**, which was formed as a **not-for-profit** company under **Section 8** of the **Companies Act 2013**.
 
• The primary objective of **iDEX** is to engage various stakeholders, including **start-ups**, **MSMEs**, **individual innovators**, and **academic institutions**, to develop cutting-edge technologies for the **Indian Armed Forces**.
 
• It provides **grants** and **funding** to carry out **Research and Development (R&D)** projects that have a high potential for future adoption by the **Indian Army**, **Navy**, and **Air Force**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO):**
 
 
• The **DIO** was founded by two major **Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs)**, namely **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)** and **Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL)**.
 
• It acts as the executive body that oversees the implementation of the **iDEX** framework and ensures the efficient utilization of the **Defence Innovation Fund**.
 
 
 
• **Technology Development Fund (TDF):**
 
 
• The **Technology Development Fund (TDF)** is a program executed by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**.
 
• It aims to support **MSMEs** and **start-ups** in developing components, products, and systems that are currently not available in the **Indian defence** industry.
 
• Unlike **iDEX**, which focuses on broader innovation, **TDF** is more specifically aligned with **DRDO's** mission of **indigenization**.
 
 
 
• **Acing Development of Innovative Technologies with iDEX (ADITI):**
 
 
• The **ADITI** scheme was launched in **March 2024** during the **DefConnect 4.0** event to promote innovations in **critical and strategic defence technologies**.
 
• It offers a much higher grant-in-aid of up to **Rs 25 crore** to **start-ups** for research and development in areas like **space technology** and **cybersecurity**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Defence India Startup Challenge (DISC):** Under the **iDEX** initiative, the **DISC** is periodically launched to present specific problem statements from the **Armed Forces** to the **start-up ecosystem**.
 
• **Self-Reliance:** The core vision of these schemes is to achieve **Atmanirbharta** (self-reliance) in **defence production** and reduce India's dependency on **foreign imports**.
 
• **iDEX Prime:** This is an extension of **iDEX** meant to support projects requiring higher funding, offering grants up to **Rs 10 crore** for more complex **technological challenges**.
 
• **Financial Support:** Since its inception, **iDEX** has supported hundreds of **start-ups** and led to the procurement of various **indigenous technologies** by the **Indian military**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following countries celebrated Poson Poya Honoring 2000 Years of Buddhism in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Lanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Poson Poya** is a major religious and cultural festival celebrated by Buddhists in **Sri Lanka** to commemorate the arrival of **Buddhism** in the country.
 
• The festival takes place annually on the **Full Moon** day of **June**, which is known as **Poson** in the **Sinhala** calendar. In **June 2025**, the nation marks this significant milestone with island-wide celebrations.
 
• It commemorates the arrival of **Arahat Mahinda**, the son of the **Indian** **Emperor Ashoka**, who brought the teachings of the **Buddha** to **Sri Lanka** in the **3rd Century BC**.
 
• The historic introduction of **Buddhism** occurred at **Mihintale**, where **Arahat Mahinda** met and converted **King Devanampiyatissa**, the reigning monarch of the time.
 
• The celebrations in **June 2025** honor the enduring legacy of over **2000 years** of Buddhist tradition, which has fundamentally shaped the **culture**, **social structure**, and **governance** of **Sri Lanka**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Significance**: 
 
 
• **Mihintale**, located near the ancient city of **Anuradhapura**, is regarded as the cradle of **Buddhism** in **Sri Lanka**. During **Poson Poya**, thousands of **pilgrims** climb the **1,840 steps** to reach the summit of the sacred mountain.
 
• **Anuradhapura**, a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, serves as the primary hub for religious observances, including **Sil** campaigns and meditation sessions.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Traditions**: 
 
 
• Devotees engage in **Amisa-puja** (offerings of food and flowers) and **Pratipatti-puja** (following the path of Dhamma). Many laypersons observe **Atthasila** (the eight precepts) while wearing **white** attire.
 
• A unique feature of the festival is the **Dansala**, where local communities provide **free food**, drinks, and snacks to **pilgrims** and travelers as an act of **generosity** (Dana).
 
• The streets are decorated with **Buddhist flags** and **illuminated lanterns**. Large structures called **Pandols** (Thoranas), depicting stories from the **Jataka tales** (previous lives of the Buddha), are erected with colorful electric lights.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**: 
 
 
• Following the meeting at **Mihintale**, **Buddhism** became the **state religion** of **Sri Lanka**. This led to the establishment of the **Mahavihara** monastery and the flourishing of **Pali literature** and **Sinhalese architecture**.
 
• The **Government of Sri Lanka** typically declares a **Poson Week** to facilitate religious activities and ensures the protection of sacred sites during the influx of **pilgrims**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Vesak**: While **Vesak** (celebrated in **May**) commemorates the **birth**, **enlightenment**, and **passing away** (Parinirvana) of the **Buddha**, **Poson** is specific to the **Sri Lankan** context, celebrating the localized birth of the **Dhamma** on the island.
 
• **National Importance**: **Poson Poya** is a **Public Holiday** in **Sri Lanka**. In **2025**, special focus is placed on **interfaith harmony** and the **preservation of ancient monuments** that date back to the initial conversion period.
 
• **Modern Observance**: Modern celebrations often include **Poson Bhakthi Gee** (devotional songs) and processions (**Peraheras**) involving traditional **dancers** and **drummers**.
</ul

questions.question: Which Gram Panchayat received the Gold Award in the new category of the National e-Governance Awards 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rohini, Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rohini Gram Panchayat**, located in the **Wardha** district of **Maharashtra**, achieved the prestigious **Gold Award** at the **National e-Governance Awards 2025** (officially presented during the **27th National Conference on e-Governance**).
 
• The award was conferred under the newly instituted **Category IX**, which focuses on **Excellence in District level initiative in e-Governance** specifically highlighting the role of **Gram Panchayats** in digital transformation.
 
• The initiative was recognized for its exemplary use of technology to streamline **administrative processes**, improve **transparency**, and provide **citizen-centric services** directly at the doorstep of rural residents.
 
• This recognition was part of the awards organized by the **Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG)** in collaboration with the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)** and the **Government of Maharashtra**.
 
• As a recipient of the **Gold Award**, the **Rohini Gram Panchayat** received a trophy, a certificate, and a substantial cash incentive of **Rs. 10 Lakhs** to further enhance its digital infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National e-Governance Awards (NAeG):**
 
 
• These awards are presented annually to recognize and promote excellence in the implementation of **e-Governance** initiatives that improve the **ease of living** for citizens.
 
• The **2025** cycle awards were showcased during the conference held in **Mumbai** in **September 2024**, reflecting the progress made during the **2024-2025** administrative year.
 
 
 
• **Category-specific Details:**
 
 
• The introduction of a specific category for **Gram Panchayats** underlines the **Government of India's** commitment to the **Digital India** mission at the grassroots level.
 
• While **Rohini, Maharashtra** secured the **Gold**, **West Malsipur Gram Panchayat** from **Tripura** was honored with the **Silver Award** in the same category.
 
 
 
• **Role of Technology in Rural Governance:**
 
 
• The **e-GramSwaraj** portal, launched by the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj**, serves as a primary tool for digital accounting and planning for these local bodies.
 
• Successful panchayats like **Rohini** utilize these platforms to ensure **100%** digital payments and real-time monitoring of development projects.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evaluation Parameters:** The selection process involves rigorous vetting based on **innovation**, **sustainability**, **scalability**, and the extent of **citizen engagement**.
 
• **Geographic Significance:** **Maharashtra** has consistently performed well in the **e-Governance** index, and the success of a village in **Wardha** signifies the penetration of **digital literacy** in the **Vidarbha** region.
 
• **Historical Context:** The **National Conference on e-Governance** has been held since **1997**, evolving from simple discussions on computerization to complex dialogues on **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and **Blockchain** in governance.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following countries won the Presidency of International Institute of Administrative Sciences for the term 2025-28?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India** won the **Presidency** of the **International Institute of Administrative Sciences (IIAS)** for the term **2025-28**. This significant victory marks a major milestone for the country in the field of global administrative reforms and public governance.
 
• The election for the Presidency took place during the **IIAS Annual Conference 2024**, which was held in **Mombasa, Kenya**, in **February 2024**. India's candidacy was strongly supported by various member nations.
 
• **S. Chockalingam**, a **1996-batch IAS officer** and the **Director General** of the **Yashwantrao Chavan Academy of Development Administration (YASHADA)** in **Pune**, was elected as the **President-elect**. He will represent India at the helm of this prestigious international body.
 
• India's victory is seen as a recognition of its robust **administrative framework** and its continuous efforts toward **digital transformation** and **citizen-centric governance**. The **Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG)**, under the **Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions**, led the institutional representation for India.
 
• With this Presidency, India will play a pivotal role in shaping the global agenda for **public administration**, fostering international cooperation, and sharing best practices in **governance** and **public policy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Institute of Administrative Sciences (IIAS):**

 
 
• Established in **1930**, the **IIAS** is a global federation headquartered in **Brussels, Belgium**.
 
• It focuses on improving **administrative sciences** and **public administration** through research, training, and the exchange of knowledge among governments and academic institutions.
 
• It currently comprises several member states, national sections, and academic entities, serving as a platform for **comparative public administration** studies.
 
 
 
• **Role of DARPG:**
 
 
• The **Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG)** is the nodal agency for the Government of India for **administrative reforms**.
 
• Under the leadership of Secretary **V. Srinivas**, the department has been actively promoting India's **administrative achievements** on international forums.
 
• The department is responsible for formulating policies for **grievance redressal**, **e-governance**, and **disseminating best practices** across various sectors.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Presidency:**
 
 
• Winning the Presidency allows **India** to lead the **Council of Administration** and the **Executive Committee** of the IIAS.
 
• It provides an opportunity for **India** to influence global **governance standards** and showcase the **"Minimum Government, Maximum Governance"** philosophy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **2025 IIAS Annual Conference:**

 
 
• As part of its rising leadership, **India** is set to host the **2025 IIAS Annual Conference** in **Kochi, Kerala**.
 
• The conference is scheduled to be held from **February 24 to 28, 2025**.
 
• The theme for the **2025 Kochi Conference** is **"Next Generation Administrative Reforms - Empowering the Citizens and Reaching the Last Mile"**.
 
• This event will bring together over **30 countries** and **administrative experts** to discuss **digital governance**, **institutional capacity building**, and **sustainable development goals (SDGs)**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• This is the **first time** an **Indian official** has been elected to the post of **President** of the **IIAS** since its inception in **1930**.
 
• India has been a member of the IIAS for decades, but this **2025-2028 term** marks its highest level of institutional involvement and leadership.

questions.question: The All India Chess Federation (AICF) launched which scheme to support young chess players from U-7 to U-19 age groups in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Top National Players Stipend Scheme**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **All India Chess Federation (AICF)** introduced the **Top National Players Stipend Scheme** in early **2025** as a landmark initiative to provide financial stability to budding chess prodigies across **India**.
 
• This scheme is specifically designed to support young players in age groups ranging from **Under-7 (U-7)** to **Under-19 (U-19)**, covering both **Open** and **Girls** categories.
 
• Under this initiative, the **top 12 players** from each national age-group championship are eligible to receive a monthly stipend, creating a pool of approximately **156 beneficiaries** annually.
 
• The financial aid is intended to cover essential expenses such as **professional coaching**, **travel for international tournaments**, and **entry fees**, helping players focus on their growth without economic pressure.
 
• The implementation of this scheme in **2025** aligns with the **AICF's** broader vision to maintain India's dominance in world chess following the country's historic **Double Gold** win at the **45th Chess Olympiad**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **All India Chess Federation (AICF):**
 
 
• Established in **1951**, the **AICF** is the central administrative body for chess in **India** and is headquartered in **New Delhi**.
 
• It is affiliated with **FIDE** (International Chess Federation) and has been instrumental in producing over **80 Grandmasters** as of **2024-2025**.
 
• The current leadership, including President **Nitin Narang** and Secretary **Dev A. Patel**, has focused on grassroots development and administrative transparency.
 
 
 
• **Chess Development in India:**
 
 
• India has emerged as a global superpower in chess, boasting world-class talents like **D Gukesh**, **Arjun Erigaisi**, and **R Praggnanandhaa**.
 
• The **Top National Players Stipend Scheme** is part of a larger **₹65 crore** budget allocated for the **2024-2025** cycle to revamp the chess ecosystem.
 
• Other recent initiatives include the **National Chess Academy** and the introduction of **Chess in Schools** programs to popularize the game at the primary level.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Stipend Schemes:**
 
 
• By providing a **stipend**, the federation aims to prevent "talent drain," where high-potential players quit the sport due to the high costs associated with **Grandmaster**-level training.
 
• This structured support system acts as a **scholarship**, rewarding consistency in **National Championships** and encouraging competitive participation at the state and district levels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Top National Players Stipend Scheme** is a merit-based system where performance in the **National Age Group Championships** serves as the sole criteria for selection.
 
• The stipend amounts are tiered, ensuring that those ranked higher (e.g., **Rank 1 to 3**) receive a more significant portion of the **financial aid** compared to those in the lower bracket of the top 12.
 
• This initiative marks the first time in **Indian Chess** history that such a large number of junior players are being brought under a direct **monthly payroll** by the national federation.
 
• The scheme also complements the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**' efforts under the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)**, which primarily focuses on senior elite athletes.

questions.question: The Air India plane that crashed in Ahmedabad in June 2025 was flying to which city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**London**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The tragic aviation incident involving an **Air India** aircraft occurred in **June 2025**.
 
• The flight was operating on a scheduled international route departing from **Ahmedabad**, **Gujarat**.
 
• The intended destination for this specific flight was **London**, **United Kingdom**, which is one of the most prominent international routes for travelers from **Western India**. ***Hence, the correct answer is London.***
 
• The aircraft involved was under the operation of **Air India**, which is the premier global airline of **India** and a member of the **Star Alliance**.
 
• The departure point was the **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport (SVPIA)**, which serves as a major hub for **Air India's** international operations in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Air India:**
 
 
• Founded by **J.R.D. Tata** in **1932** as **Tata Airlines**, it was later nationalized and eventually returned to the **Tata Group** in **January 2022**.
 
• The airline operates a massive fleet of **Boeing** and **Airbus** aircraft, providing connectivity to over **80** destinations across the **world**.
 
 
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport:**
 
 
• Located in **Ahmedabad**, it is the busiest airport in the state of **Gujarat**.
 
• The airport handles significant traffic to **European** and **Middle Eastern** countries due to the large **Gujarati diaspora** residing abroad.
 
 
 
• **Aviation Safety and Investigation:**
 
 
• Accidents of this nature are investigated by the **Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB)** in **India**.
 
• Global aviation standards are set by the **International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)**, a specialized agency of the **United Nations**.
 
 
 
• **London Heathrow (LHR):**
 
 
• The primary destination for many flights from **India**, **Heathrow** is one of the world's busiest airports and a central node for **trans-Atlantic** travel.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Flight Data Recorder (FDR):** Also known as a **black box**, this device preserves the history of the flight through the recording of dozens of parameters collected several times per **second**.
 
• **Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR):** This is used to record the audio environment in the **flight deck**, which is critical for investigators to understand the pilot's actions and communications during an emergency.
 
• **DGCA (Directorate General of Civil Aviation):** This is the statutory body of the **Government of India** that regulates civil aviation in **India** and maintains safety standards for all **Indian** registered aircraft.
</ul

questions.question: Who became the youngest player ever to win a WTA 1000 title on 22 February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mirra Andreeva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **22 February 2025**, **Mirra Andreeva** became the youngest player in history to win a **WTA 1000** title.
 
• The record-breaking victory occurred at the **Dubai Duty Free Tennis Championships**, which is a prestigious **hard-court** tournament held in the **United Arab Emirates**.
 
• At the time of her triumph, **Mirra Andreeva** was approximately **17 years and 300 days old**, surpassing the previous benchmarks set by other teenage stars in the **WTA 1000** category.
 
• This victory marked her **first career WTA 1000 title**, propelling her into the **Top 10** of the **WTA Rankings** for the first time in her career.
 
• Her run to the title involved defeating several established **Grand Slam** champions and top-seeded players, solidifying her reputation as a generational talent in professional tennis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **WTA 1000 Tournaments:** 
 
 
• These represent the highest tier of women's professional tennis events organized by the **Women's Tennis Association (WTA)**, second only to the **Grand Slams** and the **WTA Finals**.
 
• Winners of these events are awarded **1000 ranking points**. Prominent **WTA 1000** venues include **Indian Wells**, **Miami**, **Madrid**, **Rome**, **Beijing**, and **Dubai**.
 
 
 
• **Mirra Andreeva:** 
 
 
• Born on **29 April 2007** in **Krasnoyarsk, Russia**, she made a rapid ascent through the professional ranks.
 
• She gained global attention in **2023** after reaching the fourth round of **Wimbledon** at just **16 years old**.
 
• Her elder sister, **Erika Andreeva**, is also a professional tennis player on the **WTA Tour**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Players:**
 
 
• **Coco Gauff** (Option 4) previously held records as one of the youngest **WTA 1000** winners when she won the **Cincinnati Open** in **2023** at the age of **19**.
 
• **Iga Świątek** (Option 1) is a dominant force in women's tennis who won her first **Grand Slam** (French Open) at age **19** in **2020** and became the **World No. 1** in **2022**.
 
• **Clara Tauson** (Option 2) is another young talent from **Denmark** known for her powerful baseline game, though she has not yet reached the record-breaking milestones achieved by **Andreeva** in the **WTA 1000** circuit as of early **2025**.
 
 
 
• **Dubai Duty Free Tennis Championships:**
 
 
• This event is a major stop on the tennis calendar and features both **ATP** and **WTA** draws.
 
• The tournament is known for its high prize money and state-of-the-art facilities at the **Aviation Club Tennis Centre**.

questions.question: In May 2025, the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) conducted combat firing (with reduced explosives) of the indigenous Multi-Influence Ground Mine with the _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Navy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **May 2025**, the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** successfully conducted a combat firing trial of the indigenous **Multi-Influence Ground Mine** in collaboration with the **Indian Navy**.
 
• The test was carried out with **reduced explosives** to validate the sophisticated **sensor systems** and **triggering mechanisms** against the actual physical signatures of naval vessels without causing structural damage to the test platforms.
 
• This state-of-the-art underwater weapon has been designed and developed by the **Naval Science and Technological Laboratory (NSTL)**, a premier laboratory of **DRDO** located in **Visakhapatnam**.
 
• The **Multi-Influence Ground Mine** is a highly advanced sea mine that can be deployed from **ships** and **submarines** to protect Indian waters and deny sea access to enemy forces. ***Hence, the correct answer is the Indian Navy.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Multi-Influence Technology:** 
 
 
• Unlike traditional contact mines, influence mines do not require physical contact with a ship's hull. They use **microprocessor-based sensors** to detect **magnetic**, **acoustic**, and **pressure** signatures of passing vessels.
 
• The mine is **programmable**, allowing it to target specific types of ships or submarines while ignoring friendly vessels or decoys, making it a "smart" underwater weapon.
 
 
 
• **Design and Production:**
 
 
• The development of this mine is a significant step toward **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-Reliant India) in the defense sector, reducing the **Indian Navy's** reliance on imported naval mines.
 
• Following successful combat trials, the technology is typically transferred to production agencies like **Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL)** for mass manufacturing.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• Sea mines are cost-effective tools for **sea denial** and **harbor defense**. They can be laid in **shipping lanes** or near **enemy ports** to restrict their naval movement during a conflict.
 
• The **Multi-Influence Ground Mine** is designed to be laid on the **seabed** (ground mine) in **shallow or medium-depth waters**, making it extremely difficult for enemy minesweepers to detect and neutralize.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technical Specifications:** The full-scale version of these mines typically carries a high-explosive warhead of approximately **480 kg to 500 kg**, capable of crippling large warships.
 
• **Operational Life:** These indigenous mines are designed with a **shelf life** of over **10 to 15 years** and can remain active on the seabed for long durations (up to **one year**) after deployment.
 
• **Safety Features:** The mines include **advanced arming and safety devices** to ensure they only become active after reaching a specific depth and after a pre-set time delay, preventing accidents during deployment by **Indian Navy** personnel.
 
• **Context of Trial:** The **May 2025** trial marks the final stages of **user validation trials** before the weapon system is formally inducted into the permanent arsenal of the **Indian Navy**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following organisations released the 8th issue of the publication titled 'EnviStats India 2025: Environment Statistics' in June 2025?

options.text: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** released the **8th issue** of the publication titled **'EnviStats India 2025: Environment Statistics'** in **June 2025**.
 
• The publication is compiled and brought out by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, which is the statistical wing of **MoSPI**. It serves as a comprehensive document providing data on various environmental indicators in **India**.
 
• **EnviStats India 2025** is prepared in accordance with the **Framework for the Development of Environment Statistics (FDES 2013)**, which was developed by the **United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD)**.
 
• The report provides essential data for monitoring the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly those related to **Clean Water and Sanitation (Goal 6)**, **Affordable and Clean Energy (Goal 7)**, and **Climate Action (Goal 13)**.
 
• The primary objective of this publication is to provide **policy-makers**, **researchers**, and **stakeholders** with reliable data on **biological resources**, **soil**, **water**, and **forest cover** to enable informed environmental decision-making.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI):**
 
 
• **MoSPI** came into existence as an independent Ministry on **15th October 1999** after the merger of the **Department of Statistics** and the **Department of Programme Implementation**.
 
• The Ministry has two wings: the **Statistics Wing** (called **NSO**) and the **Programme Implementation Wing**.
 
• It is headquartered in **New Delhi** and is responsible for the coverage and quality aspects of statistics released in the country.
 
 
 
• **EnviStats India Series:**
 
 
• The first issue of **EnviStats India** was released in **2018**. It marked a shift towards structured environmental accounting in **India**.
 
• The series follows the **System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA)** framework, which helps in understanding the interactions between the **economy** and the **environment**.
 
• It covers **six components** of environment statistics: Environmental Conditions and Quality, Environmental Resources and their Use, Residuals, Extreme Events and Disasters, Human Settlements and Environmental Health, and Environmental Protection, Management and Engagement.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC):**
 
 
• This Ministry is the nodal agency in the administrative structure of the Central Government for the planning, promotion, co-ordination and overseeing the implementation of **India's environmental and forestry policies**.
 
• While **MoEFCC** implements policies like the **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)**, the specialized statistical reporting on the environment is primarily handled by **MoSPI**.
 
 
 
• **National Green Tribunal (NGT):**
 
 
• The **NGT** is a specialized body set up under the **National Green Tribunal Act (2010)** for effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to **environmental protection**.
 
• It is a **judicial body** and does not traditionally publish the **EnviStats** statistical reports, which are the mandate of the national statistical system.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Asset Accounts:** The **8th issue** includes detailed **Asset Accounts** for **Forests**, **Land**, and **Water**, following the **SEEA Central Framework**.
 
• **Data Sources:** The data in the publication is sourced from various specialized agencies like the **Forest Survey of India (FSI)**, **Central Water Commission (CWC)**, and **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**.
 
• **Global Alignment:** By utilizing the **FDES 2013**, **India** ensures its environment statistics are comparable at an international level, assisting in global environmental monitoring reports.
</ul

questions.question: According to Union Budget 2025–26, which state will get a new Greenfield Airports as part of infrastructure development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Union Budget 2025–26**, presented by the **Finance Minister** in **February 2025**, a major emphasis was placed on the infrastructure development of **Bihar** under the **"Purvodaya"** plan.
 
• The **Government of India** announced the development of **new Greenfield Airports** in **Bihar** to improve regional air connectivity and boost economic growth in the eastern part of the country. ***Hence, the correct option is Bihar.***
 
• Specifically, the budget proposed the establishment of **three new Greenfield Airports** at **Purnea**, **Bhagalpur**, and **Rajgir**.
 
• This initiative aims to cater to the increasing passenger traffic and support the **Buddhist Circuit**, which attracts international tourists to the state.
 
• The total financial support for various **infrastructure projects** in **Bihar**, including these airports, roads, and power plants, is part of a **special package** to transform the state into an industrial hub.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Greenfield Airports:**
 
 
• A **Greenfield Airport** is a new airport constructed from scratch on previously undeveloped land or **"green" land**.
 
• Unlike **Brownfield** projects, which involve the expansion or upgrading of existing facilities, Greenfield projects allow for **modern planning**, advanced **environmental standards**, and state-of-the-art **infrastructure**.
 
• The **Government of India** has a **Greenfield Airports (GFA) Policy, 2008**, which provides guidelines for the establishment of such airports across the **country**.
 
 
 
• **Purvodaya Initiative:**
 
 
• The **Purvodaya** scheme is aimed at the **comprehensive development** of the **eastern states** of India, including **Bihar**, **Jharkhand**, **West Bengal**, **Odisha**, and **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• It focuses on making this region an **engine of growth** for the nation through investments in **human capital**, **infrastructure**, and **industrial opportunities**.
 
 
 
• **UDAN Scheme:**
 
 
• The **Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik (UDAN)** is a regional airport development and **"Regional Connectivity Scheme" (RCS)** of the **Government of India**.
 
• Launched in **2016**, it aims to make **air travel affordable** and widespread, particularly connecting **unserved** and **underserved** airports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Impact in Bihar:**
 
 
• The **Purnea airport** is expected to serve the **Seemanchal region**, providing a vital link for **trade** and **commerce** near the borders of **Nepal** and **West Bengal**.
 
• The development in **Rajgir** is strategically linked to **religious tourism**, as it is a significant site for **Buddhists**, **Jains**, and **Hindus**.
 
• The **Airports Authority of India (AAI)** will play a central role in the **technical planning** and **operationalization** of these new sites.
 
 
 
• **Multimodal Connectivity:**
 
 
• The airport projects are integrated with the **PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan**, ensuring that they are well-connected to **highways** and **railways** for seamless **logistics**.
 
• The **Union Budget 2025–26** also allocated funds for the **Patna-Purnea Expressway** and other road projects to complement the **aviation infrastructure**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Who became the first female and first African President of the IOC in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kirsty Coventry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kirsty Coventry** was elected as the **President** of the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** in **March 2025**, marking a historic milestone in sports administration.
 
• She is the **first female** and the **first African** individual to serve as the **President** of the **IOC** since its establishment in **1894**. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• The election was conducted during the **143rd IOC Session**, which was held in the symbolic location of **Ancient Olympia**, **Greece**.
 
• She succeeded **Thomas Bach**, who served as the **IOC President** from **2013** until **2025**. **Thomas Bach** reached the term limit after serving an initial **eight-year term** and a subsequent **four-year term**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Other prominent candidates considered for the position included **Sebastian Coe** (the head of World Athletics) and **Juan Antonio Samaranch Jr.** (IOC Vice President). ***Hence, statements 2 and 3 are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kirsty Coventry's Athletic Career:**
 
 
• She is the most decorated **Olympian** from the continent of **Africa**, having won a total of **seven Olympic medals**.
 
• Her achievements include **two gold medals** in the **200m backstroke**, won at the **2004 Athens Olympics** and the **2008 Beijing Olympics**.
 
• In **Zimbabwe**, she is celebrated as the "**Golden Girl**" for her immense contribution to the country's sporting legacy.
 
 
 
• **Role in Administration:**
 
 
• Before her presidency, she served as the **Minister of Youth, Sport, Arts and Recreation** in the **Government of Zimbabwe**, appointed in **September 2018**.
 
• She became an **IOC member** in **2013** and chaired the **IOC Athletes' Commission** from **2018 to 2021**, representing the voice of athletes worldwide.
 
 
 
• **About the International Olympic Committee (IOC):**
 
 
• The **IOC** is a **non-governmental**, **non-profit** organization based in **Lausanne**, **Switzerland**.
 
• It is the supreme authority of the **Olympic Movement** and is responsible for the supervision of the **Summer**, **Winter**, and **Youth Olympic Games**.
 
• The **IOC President** is elected by the **IOC Session** via a secret ballot and serves as the primary legal representative of the organization.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Election Context:** The **2025 election** was highly anticipated as it signaled a shift toward **gender parity** and **global representation** at the highest levels of sports governance.
 
• **Term Duration:** Under the **Olympic Charter**, the **President** is elected for a **first term of eight years** and can be re-elected for **one additional term of four years**.
 
• **Geographic Diversity:** Prior to **Kirsty Coventry**, the **IOC** had been led almost exclusively by **Europeans** (with the exception of **Avery Brundage** from the **USA**). Her election represents a significant breakthrough for **Global South** nations.
 
• **Responsibilities:** As **President**, Coventry will oversee the preparations for the **2028 Los Angeles Olympics** and the **2032 Brisbane Olympics**, while navigating the challenges of **digital transformation** and **sustainability** in sports.
</ul

questions.question: The AI Action Summit, co-chaired by France and India, was held in February 2025 at which iconic venue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Grand Palais, Paris**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **AI Action Summit** was held on **February 10-11, 2025**, in **Paris**, **France**, at the iconic **Grand Palais**.
 
• The summit was co-chaired by **France** and **India**, marking a significant milestone in international cooperation for **Artificial Intelligence** governance and innovation.
 
• This event followed the trajectory of previous global gatherings, specifically the **AI Safety Summit** held at **Bletchley Park**, **UK** in **2023**, and the **AI Seoul Summit** in **South Korea** in **2024**.
 
• The primary objective of the **2025 summit** was to move beyond theoretical safety concerns toward concrete "Action," focusing on the inclusive and sustainable deployment of **AI technologies** worldwide.
 
• **India’s** role as a co-chair underscores its growing influence in the digital economy and its leadership within the **Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence (GPAI)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Venue - Grand Palais:**
 
 
• The **Grand Palais** is a historic site located on the **Champs-Élysées** in **Paris**, originally built for the **Exposition Universelle** of **1900**.
 
• Known for its massive glass roof and iron structure, it recently underwent extensive renovations and served as a major venue for the **Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games**.
 
• Hosting the **AI Action Summit** at this venue symbolized the union of historic European heritage with the cutting-edge future of **technology**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of AI Summits:**
 
 
• **Bletchley Park (2023):** The inaugural summit where the **Bletchley Declaration** was signed by **28 countries**, focusing on "frontier AI" risks.
 
• **Seoul Summit (2024):** This summit expanded the focus to include **AI safety**, innovation, and inclusivity, resulting in the **Seoul Declaration**.
 
• **Paris Summit (2025):** Emphasized **Global Governance** and the practical application of **AI** to solve real-world problems like climate change and healthcare.
 
 
 
• **The Five Pillars of the Paris Summit:**
 
 
• The discussions were structured around five themes: **AI for Public Interest**, **Future of Work**, **Innovation and Culture**, **Safety and Trust**, and **Global AI Governance**.
 
• A major focus was placed on ensuring that **Artificial Intelligence** benefits the **Global South**, preventing a widening **digital divide**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India-France Strategic Partnership:**
 
 
• The co-chairing of the summit is a result of the **Horizon 2047** roadmap signed between **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** and **President Emmanuel Macron**.
 
• The two nations have collaborated deeply on **Supercomputing**, **Quantum Computing**, and **Digital Sovereignty**.
 
 
 
• **Global Governance:**
 
 
• Participants at the **Grand Palais** discussed the alignment of the **European Union's AI Act** with other international frameworks to create a unified standard for **ethical AI**.
 
• The summit advocated for the establishment of an international scientific network for **AI safety**, similar to the **IPCC** for climate change.

questions.question: What was the unemployment rate for youth aged 15–29 in April 2025, as per Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12.3%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** data, the **Unemployment Rate (UR)** for youth in the age group of **15–29 years** in urban areas was recorded at **12.3%** for the period of **April 2025**.
 
• The survey is conducted and released by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, which functions under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** of the **Government of India**.
 
• The quarterly bulletins of the **PLFS** primarily focus on **urban areas** and utilize the **Current Weekly Status (CWS)** to estimate labor market indicators. ***Hence, the data point of 12.3% is specific to the youth urban segment during this timeframe.***
 
• A person is classified as **unemployed** under the **CWS** if they did not work for even **one hour** during the reference period of **seven days** preceding the survey but were available for and seeking work.
 
• Monitoring the youth unemployment rate (ages **15 to 29**) is crucial for the government to evaluate the effectiveness of employment generation programs and the absorption of the **demographic dividend** into the formal and informal sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):** 
 
 
• The **PLFS** was launched by the **NSO** in **April 2017** to provide more frequent labor force data. 
 
• Before its inception, the **National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO)** used to conduct **Employment and Unemployment Surveys** every five years.
 
 
 
• **Unemployment Rate (UR):** 
 
 
• It is defined as the percentage of persons unemployed among the total persons in the **Labour Force**.
 
• Formula: **UR = (Unemployed Persons / Labour Force) × 100**.
 
 
 
• **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR):** 
 
 
• The **LFPR** represents the percentage of the population that is either working (employed) or actively seeking work (unemployed). 
 
• In recent years, India has seen a steady increase in **LFPR**, particularly among **females** in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Worker Population Ratio (WPR):** 
 
 
• The **WPR** is the percentage of employed persons in the total population. It serves as an indicator of the **employment level** in the economy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Current Weekly Status (CWS):** This approach determines the activity status based on a reference period of the **last 7 days**. It is considered a more dynamic measure of unemployment compared to the **Usual Status** (which looks at the last **365 days**).
 
• **Classification of Employment:** The **PLFS** categorizes workers into **self-employed** (including own-account workers and unpaid helpers), **regular wage/salaried employees**, and **casual labor**.
 
• **Policy Impact:** The **12.3%** figure for youth unemployment highlights the necessity for targeted interventions like the **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)** and the **Atmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana** to boost job creation in the **urban service** and **manufacturing sectors**.
 
• **Quarterly vs Annual:** While the **Quarterly Bulletins** cover only **urban areas** using **CWS**, the **Annual Reports** of **PLFS** cover both **rural and urban** sectors using both **Usual Status** and **CWS** methodologies.
</ul
